proof.text: Relabel the statement's rings as $A\to B\to C$. Use the four small identity-cover sites, the functors $u_i$, the variable rings $\mathcal O^{(i)},\mathcal O_i$, and the augmentations of [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek]. Put $F_1=F_{B/A}$, $F_2=F_{C/A}$, $F_3=F_{C/B}$ as in [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model]; these are modules over the constant rings $B,C,C$, respectively. On $\mathcal E$ put $M_1=g_1^{-1}F_1\otimes_{\underline B}\underline C$, $M_2=g_2^{-1}F_2$, $M_3=g_3^{-1}F_3$. At $U=(P\to B,Q\to C)$ their values are $\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P C$, $\Omega_{Q/A}\otimes_Q C$, and $\Omega_{Q\otimes_P B/B}\otimes_{Q\otimes_P B}C$. The base-change isomorphism identifies the last with $\Omega_{Q/P}\otimes_Q C$ and sends $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ to $\mathrm dq\otimes c$. Tensor products and exactness on these sites are sectionwise since every presheaf is a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), definition of the three differential sheaves and objectwise identifications

proof.text: Choose polynomial coordinates $P=A[x_s]$, $Q=P[y_t]$. The polynomial differential-basis lemma identifies $Q\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$ with $\bigoplus_s Q\,\mathrm dx_s$, $\Omega_{Q/A}$ with $(\bigoplus_s Q\,\mathrm dx_s)\oplus(\bigoplus_t Q\,\mathrm dy_t)$, and $\Omega_{Q/P}$ with $\bigoplus_t Q\,\mathrm dy_t$. The differential maps are inclusion of the first summand and projection to the second, hence the sequence is split exact. After tensoring over $Q$ with $C$ it is still the same inclusion/projection sequence over $C$, without any flatness of $C$ over $Q$. Although these coordinate splittings are not natural, the two maps are natural: for compatible algebra maps $p\mapsto p'$, $q\mapsto q'$, both composites take $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm dp'\otimes c$, and $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to $\mathrm dq'\otimes c$ modulo base differentials. These formulas respect the differential relations and every restriction map. Thus $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{a}M_2\xrightarrow{b}M_3\to0$ is a canonical short exact sequence of $\underline C$-modules on $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), objectwise polynomial argument; Algebra Tag 00RX

proof.text: The category bar lemma gives a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to K_{\mathcal E}(M_1)\xrightarrow{K(a)}K_{\mathcal E}(M_2)\xrightarrow{K(b)}K_{\mathcal E}(M_3)\to0$ representing the result of $L\pi_!^C$. Apply the short-exact-complex triangle lemma in $\operatorname{Mod}(C)$: its boundary $\delta$ makes this a distinguished triangle in $D(C)$, natural in maps of these three complexes. Thus the boundary is fixed by this short exact sequence construction, rather than chosen by a triangle-existence axiom.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), applying derived lower shriek; sites-cohomology Tag 08PG

proof.text: Use the specific maps $c_i$ of the lower-shriek lemma with coefficient ring $C$. They identify $L\pi_!^C M_2$ and $L\pi_!^C M_3$ with $L\pi_{2,!}^C F_2$ and $L\pi_{3,!}^C F_3$; the maps $\theta$ of the sheaf-model lemma identify these with $L_{C/A}$ and $L_{C/B}$. Precomposition commutes sectionwise with tensor, so $M_1=g_1^{-1}(F_1\otimes_B C)$. Accordingly $c_1$ identifies its derived colimit with $L\pi_{1,!}^C(F_1\otimes_B C)$. For each polynomial $P=A[x_s]$, $F_1(P)=\bigoplus_s B\,\mathrm dx_s$ by the basis lemma. Tensoring any short exact sequence of $B$-modules with this module is a direct sum of that sequence and remains exact, so every value is flat. The flat-presheaf clause of the derived-colimit change-of-rings lemma now applies: its canonical bar-tensor identification gives $L\pi_{1,!}^C(F_1\otimes_B C)\simeq(L\pi_{1,!}^B F_1)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$. Finally $\theta_{B/A}\otimes1$ identifies this with $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$. No flatness of $B\to C$ was used.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), identification of all three terms; sites-cohomology Tag 08Q8

proof.text: Identify the first arrow. Let $h_1:\mathcal C_{B/A}\to\mathcal C_{C/A}$ send $(P\to B)$ to $(P\to C)$. The maps $P\to Q$ define a natural transformation $\eta_1:u_2\Rightarrow h_1u_1$ in the opposite categories. Under restriction of $F_2$ along $\eta_1$, the identity identification $M_1(U)=F_2(h_1u_1U)$ is sent to $a_U:\mathrm dp\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes c$ in $\Omega_{Q/A}\otimes_Q C$. The natural-transformation clause of the bar lemma therefore gives the equality $c_2 K(a)=K(h_1,t_1)c_1$ in $D(C)$, where $t_1:F_1\otimes_B C\to h_1^{-1}F_2$ is the identity on the displayed differential values. The change-of-rings comparison identifies $K(h_1,t_1)$ with the scalar-extended canonical sheaf-model map for the square $(A\to B)\to(A\to C)$: its generator formula is $\mathrm dp\otimes r\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes rc$. By the sheaf-model comparison identity this becomes the standard map $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}$. Thus the first arrow agrees with the required functoriality map, with the equality established by a bar homotopy rather than presumed from object isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), agreement of standard and sheaf maps; Tag 08QU, first differential map

proof.text: Identify the second arrow. Let $h_2:\mathcal C_{C/A}\to\mathcal C_{C/B}$ send $(Q\to C)$ to $(Q\otimes_A B\to C)$. The algebra quotient $Q\otimes_A B\to Q\otimes_P B$ defines a natural transformation $\eta_2:u_3\Rightarrow h_2u_2$. The sheaf-model transformation $t_2:F_2\to h_2^{-1}F_3$ sends $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$. Restricting along $\eta_2$ sends this to $b_U(\mathrm dq\otimes c)$ in the value of $M_3$. The bar natural-transformation identity gives $c_3 K(b)=K(h_2,t_2)c_2$ in $D(C)$. The sheaf-model lemma identifies $K(h_2,t_2)$ with the standard functoriality map for the square $(A\to C)\to(B\to C)$, namely $L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}$. This construction uses a tensor-product quotient, which exists for every $B\to C$; it does not require the injective-case resolution of Remark explicit-map.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), square changing the base from A to B; Tag 08QU, second differential map

proof.text: For an arbitrary commutative diagram $(A\to B\to C)\to(A'\to B'\to C')$, write its ring maps as $a_0,b_0,c_0$. Define $v:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ by $P'=P\otimes_A A'$, $Q'=Q\otimes_A A'$, with augmentations $P'\to B'$ and $Q'\to C'$ induced by the diagram; $Q'$ is polynomial over $P'$. Define $v_1(P)=P\otimes_A A'$, $v_2(Q)=Q\otimes_A A'$, $v_3(S)=S\otimes_B B'$. Then $u'_1v=v_1u_1$, $u'_2v=v_2u_2$, and $u'_3v\cong v_3u_3$ via $(Q\otimes_A A')\otimes_{P\otimes_A A'}B'\cong Q\otimes_P B'\cong(Q\otimes_P B)\otimes_B B'$. At each $U$ the three semilinear coefficient maps send $\mathrm dp\otimes c$, $\mathrm dq\otimes c$, and $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ to their primed differentials tensored with $c_0(c)$. Their two squares with $a_U,b_U$ commute by these formulas. They therefore define a map of the three bar complexes (target restricted to $C$) and a morphism of their short exact sequences. Applying the short-exact-complex triangle lemma gives $T_1[1]\delta=\delta'T_3$, where $T_i$ are these explicit bar maps.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality) and sites-cohomology Tag 08PH; arbitrary-diagram construction for Tag 08QX

proof.text: Let $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$ denote the term isomorphisms of step 4 and use primes for the target diagram. The bar formulas give $c'_iT_i=K(v_i,t_i)c_i$: both sides send the summand on $U_n\to\cdots\to U_0$ to that on $u'_ivU_n\to\cdots\to u'_ivU_0$, with the same primed differential coefficient. For $i=3$ insert the displayed tensor-associativity identification; the last clause of the bar lemma gives the same derived map. The sheaf-model identities then give $\alpha'_jT_j=f_j\alpha_j$ for $j=2,3$, where $f_2,f_3$ are the standard maps for $(A,C)\to(A',C')$ and $(B,C)\to(B',C')$. For $j=1$ use also the change-of-rings compatibility: on a bar tensor generator it sends $x\otimes c$ to $t_1(x)\otimes c_0(c)$ on both sides, so $f_1$ is the map $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{B'/A'}\otimes_{B'}^{\mathbf L}C'$ induced by the standard cotangent map and the coefficient maps. Transport the boundary as $\partial=\alpha_1[1]\delta\alpha_3^{-1}$. The preceding identities and step 7 give $f_1[1]\partial=\partial'f_3$ explicitly. The first two squares follow from their identified functoriality maps. Identities and composition follow from the same bar generator rule and the standard-resolution identities. This proves naturality of the whole canonical distinguished triangle, including its boundary, for arbitrary diagrams. Relabel $B,C$ back to $P,B$ to obtain the triangle for $A\to P\to B$.

title: Transitivity triangle for ring cotangent complexes
statement: Let $A\to P\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. With the standard cotangent complexes of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], there is a canonical distinguished triangle $L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B\to L_{B/A}\to L_{B/P}\to(L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B)[1]$ in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The first two arrows are the standard functoriality arrows for the ring maps. The triangle is natural under commutative diagrams of triples of ring maps.
